questions.question:
1. Define the following terms (6 marks)
  a) Chemical equiliBrium
  b) Phenol
  c) Carbohydrate
questions.answer_guide:
a) The state of a reversible reaction in which the forward and backward reaction rates are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products stay constant.
b) An aromatic compound in which a hydroxyl group (–OH) is attached directly to a benzene ring (C₆H₅OH).
c) Organic compounds of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen with general formula Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ – polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones (sugars, starch, cellulose).

questions.section: SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (60 MARKS)
questions.question:
5. Answer the following questions:
  a. What are the possibilities of the chemical reactions (3 marks)?
  b. calculate the kc from the following equilibrium concentrations for the reaction HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) ⇌ NaCl + H₂O(l): (3 Marks)
     [HCl] = 3.2 M   [NaOH] = 4.3 M   [NaCl] = 6.0 M   [H₂O] = 1 M
  c. Does this reaction is product favored or reactant favored? (1marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. A reaction may: go to completion (forward only); be reversible and reach equilibrium; and at equilibrium be product-favoured (Kc > 1), reactant-favoured (Kc < 1) or have comparable amounts of both (Kc ≈ 1). [Wording of this question is unclear – check against the official key.]
b. Kc = [NaCl][H₂O] / ([HCl][NaOH]) = (6.0 × 1) / (3.2 × 4.3) = 6.0 / 13.76 ≈ 0.44
c. Kc < 1, so the reaction is reactant favoured.

a. Group 16 (VIA) – the oxygen family (chalcogens).

questions.section: SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (60 MARKS)
questions.question:
7. Draw the structure of dipeptide formed by the following amino acids:
  a. H₂N–CH₂–COOH (Glycine) + H₂N–CH(CH₃)–COOH (Alanine) → (4 marks)
  b. Name the dipeptide formed (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. H₂N–CH₂–CO–NH–CH(CH₃)–COOH + H₂O (the –COOH of glycine joins the –NH₂ of alanine, forming a peptide bond –CO–NH– and eliminating water).
b. Glycylalanine (Gly-Ala).

questions.section: SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (60 MARKS)
questions.question: 8. List the factors affecting rate of reactions? (5 marks)
questions.answer_guide: Concentration (or pressure for gases); temperature; surface area (particle size); catalyst; nature of the reactants (also light for some reactions).

questions.section: SECTION D: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (60 MARKS)
questions.question:
9. Answer the following questions which are relevant to the ketones:
  a. Define ketone? (2 marks)
  b. What are the products formed when ketones are reduced? (2 marks)
  c. The simplest ketone is called Dimethyl ketone. describe its other name? (1 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Organic compounds containing a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms (R–CO–R′).
b. Secondary alcohols.
c. Acetone (propanone).
